sections.h2: What sort of place is Jeff Davis County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Jeff Davis County is farm and timber country in the southeast part of the state. Hazlehurst is the biggest town and the seat, Denton is the only other incorporated city, and the legislature created the county on August 18, 1905, according to Wikipedia.

Of its 335 square miles, 331 are land. Cotton and peanuts are the main crops, tobacco used to matter more, and timber is still a steady product. Neighbors are Wheeler, Montgomery, Toombs, Appling, Bacon, Coffee and Telfair counties. Rain here sheds several directions: the north and part of the west edge toward the Lower Ocmulgee, the eastern corner into the Altamaha, and the south toward the Little Satilla and Satilla.

Satilla is a census-designated place, and Roper, Snipesville and Tallahassee are unincorporated crossroads. A sale in Hazlehurst, a country house near one of those crossroads and a cut-over timber tract each reach a different pool of buyers.

sections.h2: How affordable is housing in Jeff Davis County?
sections.html:
Very. QuickFacts reports a middle value of $118,300 for owner-occupied homes in 2020-2024, and 71.3% of homes are lived in by their owners.

Headcount rose to 15,068 in 2010, eased to 14,779 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 3.0% above that last figure. One third of occupied homes (33.1%) were rentals in the 2020 census, and 9.4% of rentals sat vacant. Nine permits in a year means almost no new homes compete with a resale, so most of what a seller competes against is other older houses.

sections.h2: Who lives in Jeff Davis County, and why should a seller care?
sections.html:
Households here are many and stable. QuickFacts counts 5,484 households with 2.70 people each, and 89.3% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most buyers will already know the area.

Under-18s make up 24.4% of the population and people 65 or older 17.0%. Only 13.2% of adults hold a bachelor's degree, while 77.3% finished high school. Broadband reaches 76.6% of households, which is worth a mention in a listing for a rural property. The county had 260 employer establishments in 2023 with total employment of 3,834, and retail sales for 2022 were $201,004,000.

Those numbers describe a buyer pool that leans local, which is why paid tax receipts and a clear title help in a market this size.

sections.h2: Where do Jeff Davis County taxpayers go with questions?
sections.html:
Start with the Tax Commissioner at 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, Hazlehurst, GA 31539, telephone (912) 375-6622. Mail goes to PO Box 558, and the counter closes at 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

  • Tax Commissioner: mails bills, collects them, issues mobile home decals, and also takes timber, heavy duty equipment and intangible tax
  • Tax Assessor, (912) 375-6624: values property and takes appeals
  • Board of Equalization: named by the Grand Jury to decide value disputes
  • Commission and school board: adopt the millage rates

The county also runs a portal for online payments. Ask the office which route fits before mailing a check close to a deadline.

sections.h2: How fast do penalties grow on a late Jeff Davis County bill?
sections.html:
They stack. Bills are normally mailed by October 20 and are payable by December 20, partial payments are accepted, and after December 20 interest is charged monthly at the bank prime rate.

A 5% penalty is then added every 120 days until the penalties reach 20%. A balance left for a year therefore costs noticeably more, and any payoff quote goes stale quickly.

  • Mobile homes: bills typically go out in January, with an April 1 due date and a decal displayed once paid
  • After April 1: a 10% filing penalty and 1% a month, then a FiFa on the clerk's docket and possible auction
  • A mobile home on the owner's own land can be homesteaded and is then taxed as real property

One more county page lists May 1 for mobile homes, so ask the office before relying on either date.

sections.h2: What does the Jeff Davis County homestead exemption cover?
sections.html:
The standard exemption is $2,000, deducted from assessed value, with the county and school taxes covered and municipal school levies and bond debt excluded.

Applications go to the Tax Commissioner's counter between January 1 and April 1, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The county states that state law allows no extension, so a missed date waives the exemption for that year. After approval it renews each year until your situation changes, and it can never exceed the tax actually owed. A larger local exemption, where one exists, replaces the State amount.

  • Conservation use and residential transitional property
  • Agricultural preferential assessment
  • Rehabilitated historic property

These three preferential programs ask the owner to sign a covenant with the Tax Assessor to keep the property in its qualifying use for at least ten years. Call (912) 375-6624 before selling enrolled land, and ask what the covenant requires of a new owner.

sections.h2: What can I do if I think my Jeff Davis County value is too high?
sections.html:
Put your objection in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice, naming the appeal method you want. Notices for real and personal property usually go out in the spring.

Four reasons are accepted: taxability, value, uniformity, or a denied exemption. Dislike of the tax rate or the size of the bill is not among them. You can also file a return from January 1 to April 1 giving your own view of market value on January 1, which gives you appeal rights if the assessors change it. Owners of mobile homes have 45 days from the day bills are mailed, and 21 days after a change notice to take the dispute to the Board of Equalization.

sections.h2: How should I prepare to sell a Jeff Davis County property with tax outstanding?
sections.html:
Request a written payoff from the Tax Commissioner and let the closing office pay it from your proceeds. Interest runs monthly and penalties jump every 120 days, so an older quote may be short.

Land with timber may carry timber tax, which the same office collects. Owners of a mobile home on rented land should check the decal and the April 1 bill before listing. A FiFa on the clerk's docket is public, so a buyer's title search can find it.

sections.h2: What do returns and spring notices involve in Jeff Davis County?
sections.html:
Taxable property has to be returned to the Tax Assessors Office between January 1 and April 1. If an owner files nothing, the county assumes the same value and the same real property exemptions as the year before.

Values come from recent sales and market conditions as of January 1, and the spring notice lists the value of each parcel. Filing your own return with a January 1 opinion of value preserves the right to appeal if the figure is changed.

  • Report a new mailing address promptly; notices go to the last address the county has
  • An exemption, once approved, keeps renewing until eligibility changes

faqs.q: When does a Jeff Davis County bill have to be paid?
faqs.a: By December 20. Bills normally go out by October 20, and part-payments are taken before the deadline.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Jeff Davis County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: (912) 375-6622, at 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, in Hazlehurst. Valuation questions go to the Tax Assessor at (912) 375-6624.

faqs.q: How much does a late Jeff Davis County bill cost?
faqs.a: Interest accrues monthly at the bank prime rate, and a 5% penalty is added every 120 days up to 20%. A late mobile home pays 10% plus 1% a month after April 1.

faqs.q: What window do Jeff Davis County owners have for homestead?
faqs.a: January 1 through April 1 for the current tax year. The county says Georgia law allows no extension.

faqs.q: How long can I wait to appeal a Jeff Davis County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date of the assessment notice. File the written appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors and name your chosen method.
